title: Binary commuting projectors attain the Schur-commutator bound 2d for every d at n=5d (follow-up to #4597 OQ2 and #4609; no new κ)
body:
A follow-up to **#4597's open question 2** and my #4609. **Over F₂, commuting projectors attain the Schur-commutator bound 2d for every d**, at n = 5d. No new κ.

## Proof

Tensor #4609's F₂ witness at n = 5, d = 1 with I_d.

- **Inputs.** P ⊗ I_d and Q ⊗ I_d are commuting idempotents with leading blocks I_d.
- **Complements.** Their Schur complements are S ⊗ I_d and Z ⊗ I_d.
- **Rank.** The commutator is [S,Z] ⊗ I_d, of rank 2d. This equals the refined bound min(2d, 2⌊4d/2⌋) = 2d.

`research/binary-projector-sharpness/verify.py` checks d = 1, …, 4. It uses the standard library only and runs in well under 1 s.

## Limitation

The minimal n is open. n = 5d suffices, but d = 2 already reaches rank 4 at n = 6 (#4609).
